eggInfo.odds:
Eggs have a 50% chance to hatch a Pokémon from your highest region, with the odds continuing to be halved for each prior region. Kanto and Johto pools will always have equal odds.

For example: in Sinnoh, there is a 50% chance to obtain Pokémon from the Sinnoh egg pool, a 25% chance to obtain Pokémon from the Hoenn egg pool, and a 12.5% chance to obtain Pokémon from both the Kanto and Johto egg pools.
eggInfo.purchase: Pokémon Eggs can be purchased or traded for in shops throughout each region and can be hatched to obtain exclusive Pokémon. Click on an egg below to view its hatching pool.

help.attackBonus: Once an egg hatches, your Pokémon will gain a bonus of {{bonus}}% of their base attack and have a higher chance of becoming shiny!
help.baseAttackNote: NOTE: Base attack is the value your Pokémon originally has at level 100, before any breeding buffs.
help.calciums: Any Calciums applied to Pokémon will give them an additional 1% of their base attack per hatch, but require 20 more steps.
help.carbos: Any Carbos applied to Pokémon will reduce the steps required per hatch.
help.helpersAttackEfficiency: They each also have different attack efficiencies, which will determine how much attack you gain compared to manually hatching the Pokémon yourself.
help.helpersBonus: These efficiencies will gain a bonus based on how many times you've used the helper to hatch eggs.
help.helpersCost: The cost displayed is how much you will be charged per hatch.
help.helpersFilters: They will only breed Pokémon based on your current Hatchery filters.
help.helpersIntro: Hatchery Helpers will help out by automatically breeding your Pokémon for you.
help.helpersMore: More Hatchery Helpers can be unlocked through shops and hatching more Pokémon
help.helpersStepEfficiency: All of the Helpers have different step efficiencies and will hatch eggs faster or slower depending on their value.
help.intro: You can leave your level 100 Pokémon here in the hatchery to gain an egg of the same Pokémon.
help.noLimit: There is no limit to breeding, so this will be your main source of attack gain.
help.proteins: Any Proteins applied to Pokémon will give them an additional 1 attack per hatch, but require 20 more steps.
help.queue: You will gain access to a queue in the hatchery once you reach the Johto region, and more queue slots for each new region reached after that.
help.shinyBonus: Hatching a shiny Pokémon will grant it 5 times the usual attack gain. Note that this bonus does not apply to every hatch of existing shiny pokemon. In other words, if you breed a shiny Pokémon, it will only receive the bonus if it hatches shiny again.

breeding.mysteryEggInfo: Mystery Eggs can hatch Pokémon from both their own exclusive pool and all other typed egg pools. The exclusive Pokémon are listed below.

noBattleItems.answer:
Disables the usage of X Attack, X Click, Lucky Egg, Token Collector, Dowsing Machine, and Lucky Incense.
You can still buy or find these items even if you can't use them.
noBattleItems.title: No Battle Items

noClickAttack.answer:
Disables the ability to use click attacks.
You still can click in the very first battle of the game.
noClickAttack.title: No Click Attack

noGemUpgrades.answer:
Disables the usage of Gems to increase damage multipliers.
You can still get gems and use them to buy items such as flutes or Pokémon.
noGemUpgrades.title: No Gem Upgrades

noMasterBalls.answer:
Disables the usage of Master Balls.
You still can buy them, so you can complete the related achievements.
noMasterBalls.title: No Master Balls

noOakItems.answer:
Disables the usage of all Oak items.
The achievements related to leveling up these items will disappear, and the percentages will be distributed among the other general achievements.
In order to get the berries that mutate while using some Oak Items you can buy them in Johto berry master once you have unlocked the berry that evolves to them.
noOakItems.title: No Oak Items

noVitamins.answer:
Disables the usage of vitamins.
You can still buy and find them, so the related achievements can still be completed. After getting them you can get a money refund by inputting the code: "REFUND-VITAMINS" (one use only).
noVitamins.title: No Vitamins

realEvolution.answer:
Your Pokémon go away when they evolve.
When your Pokémon evolve their stats are carried over to the evolution. This includes times hatched, EVs, and shiny status.
If the base Pokémon had a Held Item, it will be carried over to the evolution unless the item is incompatible. For example, Light Ball won't be transferred to a Raichu but a Magnet will.
Baby Pokémon aren't considered evolutions but gifts.
realEvolution.title: Real Evolution

regionalDebuff.answer:
Lowers the attack of Pokémon that aren't native to the current region.
The strength of the debuff is based on your highest region, not the region you are battling in.
Pokémon retain 20% of their attack in Johto and this value raises by 10% each region.
Note: This challenge is activated by default.
regionalDebuff.title: Regional Attack Debuff

requireDex.answer:
Requires a complete regional Pokédex before moving on to the next region.
You only need one of each Pokémon to be able to move to the next region. Any form of the Pokémon is valid even if it isn't the base form.
Note: This challenge is activated by default.
requireDex.title: Require Complete Pokédex

rewards.answer: You don't get anything special for having challenges active, but each challenge will give you a ribbon on your trainer profile.

slowEvs.answer:

If the challenge is deactivated, the EVs will get multiplied back.

damage.answer:
The damage you do against an enemy Pokémon is the sum of the attack of all Pokémon the player has, after type effectiveness, type weakness, and other multipliers are applied.
For players' Pokémon with two types, only the most efficient type is applied
For enemy Pokémon with two types, effectiveness and weakness is applied once to each type.
For enemy Pokémon with one type, effectiveness and weakness is applied twice to that single type.
Other factors that will multiply damage value include flutes, battle items, and weather. Gems can be used to change the effectiveness and weakness multipliers as well.
Player can check the attack against a specific Pokémon they are fighting by hovering over Pokémon attack value.
damage.question: How is damage calculated?

berriesUse.answer:
These items can be used in the Farm to grow more berries and earn farm points.
They can be exchanged for different items or Pokémon in Berry Master Shops.
They have special Auras that can provide Gameplay bonuses.
They can attract wild Pokémon to the Farm that can be captured, some of which can only be obtained this way.

evolutionItems.answer: You can use evolution items by clicking Items in the Start Menu.
evolutionItems.question: How do I evolve Pokémon that require an item to evolve?

moreBerries.answer:

The Kanto Berry Master in Cerulean City will provide daily hints about how to mutate the various berries.

oakItemSlots.question: How many Oak Item slots are available?

restores.answer: They can be used in the underground to restore energy.
restores.question: What is the small/medium/large restore used for?

evBonus.answer: The EV damage multiplier is multiplicative, and scales linearly until 1.5x (50 EVs). The bonus thereafter has diminishing returns relative to the number of EVs gained, but has no limit.
evBonus.question: What is the EV Attack Bonus?

gainEvs.answer:
EVs can be gained in a variety of ways, but are primarily gained by capturing (not breeding) Pokémon.
You can use the Contagious Poké Ball selector (unlocked after getting Pokérus) to focus catching Pokémon with less than 50 EVs. Note that setting this selector to "Do not catch" will prevent you from catching any Contagious Pokémon, even if your Caught selector has a Poké Ball set.

Base Yield: 0.1EV
Base Wanderer Yield: 0.2EV
Wanderer Yield: 1EV
Evolution Item / Shopmon / Safari Yield: 1EV
Shadow Modifier: 2×
Shiny Modifier: 5×
Dungeon Modifier: 3×
Dungeon Mimic / Dungeon Boss Modifier: 10×
Roamer Modifier: 50×
Repeat Ball Modifier: 5×
Macho Brace Modifier: 1.5×
Power Bracer Modifier: 2×
Rowap Aura Modifier: Multiplier based off Farm Setup
Blue Flute Modifier: % based off Achievement Bonus
gainEvs.question: How do I gain EVs?

spread.answer: Pokérus is spread by Pokémon that are infected, to other Pokémon in the hatchery (not in the queue) that share a type with the infected Pokémon. Neither Pokémon can be ready to hatch, nor can a Hatchery Helper be used on either Pokémon.
spread.question: How do I spread Pokérus?

statusFilters.answer:
None: Pokémon that have not been infected with Pokérus.
Infected: Pokémon has Pokérus, but cannot spread Pokérus or gain EVs until hatching.
Contagious: Pokémon with less than 50 EVs.
Resistant: Pokémon with 50 or more EVs. These Pokémon will still be able to spread Pokérus.
statusFilters.question: What do the Pokérus status filters mean?

unlockEvs.answer: EVs are unlocked after defeating the Distortion World dungeon in Sinnoh.
unlockEvs.question: When do I unlock EVs?

whatIs.answer: Pokérus is a beneficial virus your Pokémon can catch. EVs, also called Effort Values, increase the attack of your Pokémon.
whatIs.question: What is Pokérus, and what are EVs?

breedShiny.answer: Yes, once a Pokémon is shiny, it will always remain shiny.
breedShiny.question: If I breed a shiny Pokémon, will it still stay shiny?

evolveShiny.answer: No, you will need to obtain the evolution's shiny via a different method.
evolveShiny.question: If I evolve a shiny Pokémon, will the evolution be shiny?

roamingOdds.answer:
The chance to encounter a roaming Pokémon is 1/8192 for the first route of a region, and increases linearly up to 1/4096 for the last route of a region.
("first" and "last" here just being the route difficulty/HP, not necessarily the order you reach the route)
roamingOdds.question: What are the odds of finding a roaming Pokémon?

shinyBonus.answer: Yes, they give an extra 100% bonus to Click Attack.
shinyBonus.question: Do shiny Pokémon give any bonus to gameplay?

In a Dungeon: 1/4096

In the Safari Zone: 1/1024
From a Shop: 1/1024

From a Reward: 1/1024

shinyOdds.question: What are the odds of finding a shiny Pokémon?

help.amazeMulch: A weaker combination of Boost, Rich and Surprise mulch.
help.boostMulch: Increases the growth rate of Berry plants.
help.farmHands: Farm Hands can help around the Farm; they will harvest and plant Berries as needed or catch wild wanderers, and accrue Farm Points while doing so.
help.farmHandsEfficiency: Efficiency refers to how many actions they can do per work cycle.
help.farmHandsEnergy: If they run out of energy, they won't do any work for that cycle, but will regenerate some energy instead. If there's no work to do currently, they will also regenerate some energy. Firing them will allow them to recover energy at the same rate as if they were still hired.
help.farmHandsMax: Up to 3 Farm Hands can be hired at a time.
help.farmHandsMore: More Farm Hands can be unlocked through shops and unlocking unique Berries.
help.freezeMulch: Stops Berry growth and auras. Mutations will still occur while Berries are frozen.
help.gooeyMulch: Boosts Wanderer catch rate by 10% and increases the chance of non-base Wanderers appearing. Available from Unova.
help.growth:
Each Berry type takes a different amount of time to grow.
Once fully grown, the Berry plant can be manually harvested with a click or by a hired Farm Hand. Both methods will yield Farm Points.
help.intro: In the farm you can plant and harvest Berries.
help.locking:
You can lock specific plots by toggling on the lock with the lock button
or using the hotkey {{hotkey}}.
You can also press Shift + Click while having any tool/Berry selected to safely lock a plot.
help.lockingEffect:
Locking a plot prevents you from planting, harvesting,
or interacting with the plot in any way.
help.lockingIgnore: Locked plots ignore Harvest All, Plant All, or Mulch All buttons as well as Farm Hand activity.
help.module:
Monitor and interact with the farm in a limited capacity without opening the full modal. Harvest or plant Berries, apply mulch, use shovels, and lock/unlock plots with the extended controls.
Hide the extended controls for less clutter while still being able to plant and harvest Berries or disable the module completely in the settings.
You can also use Shift + Click to safely lock/unlock a plot.
The Farm shortcut will be hidden when the Farm module is enabled.
help.mulchEffects: They can be used on plots for different effects:
help.mulchShovels: If you want to remove a mulch, you can use Mulch Shovels. Using one will remove the full mulch effect, regardless of the time remaining.
help.mulches: Mulches can be bought in later regions from Berry Masters. They last 5 minutes each and can be stacked. However, you cannot combine multiple types of mulch on the same plot!
help.mutationKinds:
Common mutations: They require specific Berries to happen. These mutations only happen at Ripe stage.
Evolution mutations: They usually require a Berry changing into other and are related with flavour profiles or use of objects. These mutations can start to happen at Taller stage.
help.mutationTypes: There are two types of mutations:
help.mutations:
Berries have the chance to cause mutations and create new Berry species in empty plots based on certain conditions.
(The Berry Master in Kanto will give you daily hints to what these conditions may be.)
help.plots: Additional plots can be unlocked by spending Berries.
help.richMulch: Increases the number of Berries harvested.
help.shovels: If you want to remove a Berry plant before it is fully grown, you can use a Shovel to uproot it. This will consume the Shovel. Using it on a ripe Berry, however, will function the same as a normal harvest, and the Shovel will not be consumed!
help.shovelsShop: (Both types of shovels can be purchased in later regions from Berry Masters.)
help.trades: Berries can be traded with Berry Masters in later regions for other useful items.
help.unlocking: You can unlock a plot by using the toggle or pressing <kbd>Shift + Click</kbd> on the plot again.
help.wandererAuras: Some Berry Auras will increase or decrease the chance of encountering Wandering Pokémon.
help.wandererCatch: Your Poké Ball Filters will be used when attempting to capture a Wanderer. Farm Hands can also be used for this by enabling their Manage Wanderers setting.
help.wandererReward: Interacting with a Wanderer will earn you Farm Points whether you catch it or not. Successfully capturing one will net you Dungeon Tokens.
help.wandererStay: When a Pokémon wanders onto your farm they will appear on a plot next to the Berry and will remain there until interacted with or will flee a couple minutes after the Berry is harvested or withers.
help.wanderers: Ripe Berry plants may attract wild Pokémon that you can then capture. Some Pokémon can only be found using certain Berry species.
help.wither:
Otherwise, after some time being fully grown, the Berry plant will wither away, dropping half of the expected Berries, though it may also be re-planted automatically.
(Farm Points are not gained when Berries wither or get replanted!)

help.configureIntro: Use this tab to add, edit, re-order, and remove Pokéball filters.
help.description: You can hover (or tap) the <button class="btn-circle btn-info float-none">ℹ</button> icon for a description of what the filter will catch.
help.hidden: Some filter options and default filters are hidden at the start of the game, and will unlock as they become relevant.
help.reorder: Filters can be re-ordered by dragging them from the bar on the left side of each filter. You can click the x on the right of each filter to remove them - this will open a confirmation box to prevent accidentally deleting one.
help.rightClick: Right click (or long press on mobile) can be used to enable/disable filters from the main screen without opening this menu.
help.testDefault: With the default catch filters, you will see that both "Caught" and "New Shiny" meet their conditions, but the "New Shiny" filter is the one used for catching. The filter furthest down in your list that matches all conditions is the one used. The highlighted filters are ones that matched the scenario.
help.testExample: For instance, if you wanted to know what is used for a shiny Rattata, when you already have a normal Rattata, you would turn on the "Shiny" and "Caught" toggles, but leave the others off.
help.testExplain: This tab will allow you to see exactly which will be chosen, for some scenario you configure with the settings in the tab.
help.testIntro: In some scenario, multiple of your filters may meet all of their conditions, but only one can be used to choose a ball for catching.
help.toggleSettings: Click the "Toggle Settings" button for a filter to configure how it works. Options listed first are all the values that are checked when catching - you can click their <button class="btn-circle btn-danger float-none">−</button> to remove these. The darker options below that are not checked. You can click their <button class="btn-circle btn-success float-none">+</button> button to include it in the filter, and choose a value it must match.
help.toggles: The "Enabled" toggle allows you to turn a filter off. Disabled filters will be grayed out in the filter list on the main game screen, and also in the Test Filters tab. The "Inverted" toggle, when turned on, will make that filter ignore any Pokémon that match its conditions, and catch all the rest.

help.baitDesc: Throwing any kind of Bait will make the Pokémon eat, and less likely to flee, but harder to catch. Berry Baits change the base rates of the Pokémon, with Razz increasing catch rate, Pinap increasing the chance an Item is dropped, and Nanab lowering flee rate. Only one Berry effect can be present at a time. Provides 5 Safari XP.

startSequence.intro:
Hello, there! Welcome to the world of Pokémon!
My name is Oak. People affectionately refer to me as the Pokémon Professor.
This world is inhabited by creatures called Pokémon!
For some people, Pokémon are pets. Other use them for battling.
As for myself… I study Pokémon as a profession.
However, your very own Pokémon legend is about to unfold!
A world of dreams and adventures with Pokémon awaits! Let's go!

starter.ambushed:
Oh No! We got ambushed by these Pokémon!
I can only hold off two! Pick the one you want to fight!
starter.cantHoldOffFour: I can't hold off all four! Please pick the Pokémon you want to fight!
starter.cantHoldOffThree: I can't hold off all three! Please pick the Pokémon you want to fight!
starter.caughtIntro:
Hm! Excellent! You have caught your first Pokémon!
This is where your journey begins.
You can progress to the next route after you have defeated 10 Pokémon.
To help you on your journey, I will give you these Key Items!
You can view all your Key Items in the start menu.

battery.charges: Each successful mining attempt will add a charge, requiring {{maxCharges}} charges to be activated. You can only gain 1 charge per {{cooldown}} second. Equipping your Cell Battery Oak Item will increase the amount of energy gained per charge.
battery.discharge: When your battery is fully charged up, you can discharge it. This discharge will leave a pattern of cleared tiles behind. With higher level patterns, which damage more tiles, becoming available as you level up.

discovery.intro: The discovery time is calculated as follows:
discovery.notRandom: Current mine is not a {{random}}: No discovery time
discovery.other: The discovery time starts at {{base}} and is reduced by {{reduction}} for every level past level {{level}}.
discovery.random:
Current mine is a {{random}}:
The discovery time starts at {{base}} and is reduced by {{reduction}} for every level past level {{level}}. This is then further reduced as you discover treasures in your current mine.
discovery.title: Discovery Time Calculation

experience.intro: Using tools and experts not only helps you gather treasures but also grants experience that helps in leveling up.
experience.levelDiscovery: Reduces the discovery time of mines when applicable
experience.levelDurability: Increases the rate at which tools gain durability
experience.levelIntro: Your underground level will affect the following:
experience.levelTreasures: Increases the minimum and maximum amount of treasures that can be found in a mine
experience.sharedExpert: Expert Actions: When the expert performs an action that gains them experience, the player will also gain {{fraction}} of that experience, rounded to the nearest tenth.
experience.sharedPlayer: Player Actions: When the player performs an action that gains experience, the active expert will also gain {{fraction}} of that experience, rounded to the nearest tenth.
experience.title: Experience and Leveling

experts.actionBomb: Bomb: When not all treasures have been seen.
experts.actionChisel: Chisel: When all treasures have been seen, and the spot that is being mined has no adjacent tiles with a reward
experts.actionHammer: Hammer: When all treasures have been seen, and the spot that is being mined has at least 1 adjacent tile with a reward
experts.energyRestore: Energy restore: An expert can use an energy potion to restore a portion of the time until they can perform their next action. When an expert is allowed to use multiple restores they will first use the best restore at their disposal.
experts.expertise: Expertise: Each expert has an expertise, a specific mine they are more likely to find.
experts.expertiseBase: Starts at {{chance}} chance to find their specific mine when searching.
experts.expertiseFallback: If they don’t find their specific mine, they will find a {{random}}.
experts.expertiseIncrease: Increases by {{increase}} per level, up to a maximum of {{maximum}}.
experts.intro: Experts are characters you can hire to assist with mining tasks. They perform actions at certain timing intervals and become more efficient as they level up. Each of them bring their own powerful tools, so their actions will not affect the durability of your tools.
experts.largeRestore: Large restore: Restores 75% of the time until the next action can be performed
experts.mediumRestore: Medium restore: Restores 50% of the time until the next action can be performed
experts.rewardRetention: Reward retention: When an expert digs up a treasure (last click), there is a chance that they will keep the treasure for themselves.
experts.rewardRetentionChance: The chance starts at {{base}} and decreases by {{decrease}} per level, down to {{minimum}}.
experts.smallRestore: Small restore: Restores 25% of the time until the next action can be performed
experts.smartToolUse: Smart tool use: Experts start out inexperienced and will pick the most efficient tool {{chance}} of the time.
experts.smartToolUseIncrease: Increases by {{increase}} per level, up to {{maximum}}.
experts.title: Experts
experts.workCycle: Work cycle: Starts at {{base}} seconds and decreases by {{decrease}} second for every level, up to a minimum of {{minimum}} seconds per action.

glossary.collected: Collected treasure: All parts of the treasure are visible to the player, the treasure has been claimed
glossary.completed: Completed Mine: All buried treasures have been collected
glossary.seen: Seen treasure: At least 1 part of the treasure is visible to the player
glossary.successfulToolUse: Successful Tool Use: A tool only counts as used if its action is successful, meaning it accomplishes its intended task (e.g., mining layers or indicating tiles)
glossary.title: Glossary

mines.finding:
A new mine can be manually found by clicking the Find mine button in the Dig tab.
Automatically starting a new mine happens in the following cases:
mines.findingExpert: An expert digs up the last treasure: If your expert has the 'Use expertise' setting enabled, it will try to find a specific mine. If this setting is disabled it will find a {{random}}.
mines.findingNote: Note: This step happens before calculating a potential discovery time
mines.findingPlayer: A player digs up the last treasure: When the 'Auto restart selected mine' toggle is enabled, the game will automatically try to find a new mine of your selected type.
mines.intro: There are six different types of mines you can search for in the Underground. Understanding their unique properties and the discovery times involved is crucial for efficient mining. The Underground Glossary can be found at the bottom of this page.
mines.special:
When you (not your expert) are searching for a mine, there is a 4% chance for the mine to be a {{special}}. This mine only contains 1 treasure, which can be any of the mega stones (if eligible) or other special treasures.
Note: The auto-restart triggered by the player digging up the last item can trigger a {{special}}.
mines.title: Mines
mines.typeDiamond: {{mine}}: Contains only treasures that can be sold for diamonds.
mines.typeFossil: {{mine}}: Contains only fossils and fossil pieces.
mines.typeGemPlate: {{mine}}: Contains only gem plate treasures that can be sold for gems.
mines.typeRandom: {{mine}}: Contains all possible treasures (except the treasure found in a {{special}})
mines.typeSpecial: {{mine}}: Can only be found when special conditions are met (see below). Contains only special items.

oakItems.cellBatteryEffect: Effect: Triggers a discharge which will clear tiles in a certain pattern, new patterns become available by levelling up Cell Battery
oakItems.cellBatteryProgress: Progress: Gains progress to level up when the player uses discharge
oakItems.explosiveChargeEffect: Effect: Increases the number of tiles the Bomb tool will mine
oakItems.explosiveChargeProgress: Progress: Gains progress to level up when finding all treasures in a mine
oakItems.title: Oak Items
oakItems.treasureScannerEffect: Effect: Has a chance to duplicate a collected treasure. Keeps attempting to duplicate until it fails a chance
oakItems.treasureScannerProgress: Progress: Gains progress to level up when finding a treasure in a mine

tools.durability: Using a tool is only possible when your tool is durable enough. When you use your tool successfully it will remove some of its durability, which will be restored over time.
tools.intro: The Underground offers {{number}} powerful tools to aid in your mining and exploration. Each tool has a unique function, and understanding how to use them effectively is crucial for maximizing your mining efficiency.
tools.overview: There are {{number}} different tools available, each with unique functions:
tools.restoreRate: The restore rate of your tools depends on your Underground level.
tools.title: Tools

trading.exception: Exception: Diamond treasures cannot be traded for other items, only sold for diamonds.
trading.intro: Trading allows you to exchange treasures within the same category. Here’s how it works:
trading.ratio: 3 to 1 Trade: Trading always follows a 3 to 1 ratio (e.g., trade 3 treasures to receive 1 new treasure).
trading.sameCategory: Same Category Trading: Trades can only be made within the same category of treasures.
trading.title: Trading
